title: CLARITY Act: Why Washington could be crypto's biggest September catalyst
body: With plenty happening in broader markets at the moment, cryptocurrencies definitely have plenty to focus on in September. Treasury yields are surging. Oil is printing above $100 again. Inflation risks are back in focus, just as the Fed will be meeting next week. However, one of the most important catalysts for Bitcoin, Ethereum and the broader crypto market may come from Washington instead. The CLARITY Act (Digital Asset Market Clarity Act), a major piece of US crypto regulation aimed at establishing clearer rules for digital assets, faces a crucial procedural vote at the Senate on 15 September. This vote will determine whether lawmakers can move forward with debating the legislation, with 60 votes needed to clear the cloture hurdle. While not talked about much, I would argue this is an issue that could have material impact on how the US crypto market operates in the years ahead. What is the CLARITY Act and why does it matter for crypto? At its core, the CLARITY Act attempts to answer a question that has hung over the crypto market for years. And that is who regulates what exactly? It is essentially a bill to establish a clear regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies and digital assets by dividing oversight between the CFTC and SEC. To keep things more simply, it is a definitive legal playbook - rather than a case-by-case one - to split tokens/cryptocurrencies into either a digital commodity or an investment contract/security.

title: What the September futures rollover means for traders, ES and NQ as examples
body: What the September futures rollover means for ES and NQ traders Every quarter, traders in the E-mini S&P 500 (ES) and E-mini Nasdaq-100 (NQ) go through a ritual that catches out newer participants more often than it should: the futures rollover. With the next quarterly expiry falling on the third Friday of September, this is a good moment to explain what is actually happening, and why it matters even if you never intend to hold a contract into expiry. Why futures expire at all Unlike a stock, which exists indefinitely, a futures contract is a promise to buy or sell an underlying asset at a set price on a set date. Index futures like ES and NQ follow a quarterly cycle: March, June, September and December, often labeled H, M, U and Z after their delivery month codes. Each contract has a finite life. As it approaches expiry, exchanges and clearing firms need traders to either close their position, take (or make) delivery in some form, or shift that position into the next contract in the cycle. For cash settled index futures like ES and NQ, there is no physical delivery, but the contract still stops trading and settles to a final price, so an open position has to move to the next quarter one way or another. Spotting the roll: volume and open interest The rollover is not a single moment dictated by the exchange. It is a gradual shift in where trading activity actually sits.

body: European natural gas prices held steady around €79/MWh on Thursday, hovering near their highest level in more than three years, as concerns mounted over the region's gas supply outlook. Storage levels across Europe remain below historical averages, while escalating tensions in the Middle East continue to disrupt LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz—a vital chokepoint for roughly 20% of global gas flows, predominantly from Qatar. In the latest flashpoint, Iran reported it had attacked 10 ships near the strait and warned it would intensify strikes if the United States continued attacks on Iranian territory, stoking fears of deeper and more prolonged supply disruptions. At the same time, planned maintenance in Norway and reduced Algerian deliveries to Italy are further constraining pipeline flows into Europe. These mounting supply risks are emerging just as Europe approaches the end of its summer storage injection season, raising the prospect of fiercer competition for global gas supplies heading into the winter months. Investors remained focused on upcoming US inflation data, which will be closely watched ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy meeting next week. title: Australia Inflation Expectations Remain Elevated
body: Australia's consumer inflation expectations held at 4.9% in September 2026, unchanged from August, underscoring persistent price pressures.
